PRODUCT REQUIREMENTS DOCUMENT
B1. Problem Statement

Enterprise knowledge is fragmented across dozens of tools; employees waste hours hunting for answers, new hires ramp slowly, decisions get lost in Slack threads, and existing search ignores permissions or returns stale results. Cortex is a self-hosted "company brain" that answers any question with cited, permission-safe answers across all company knowledge — including meetings and video.

B2. Personas & Jobs-to-be-Done
IC Engineer: "Why was this architecture decision made?" → decision + PR + thread.
PM: "What's the status of feature X across Jira, Slack, meetings?"
Support Agent: "Has this customer issue been solved before?"
Exec: "Summarize what happened on project Y this week."
New Hire: "Who owns billing? Where are the runbooks?"
IT Admin: configure connectors, monitor sync health, manage models.
Security/Compliance Officer: audit access, set redaction/DLP rules, prove permission-parity.
B3. Competitive Positioning
vs Glean/Dust (SaaS, not self-hostable): Cortex is fully self-hosted in customer cloud/air-gapped.
vs Onyx (closest OSS analog, MIT core, 40+ connectors, permission-aware): Cortex adds first-class video/audio RAG, a temporal memory/decisions layer, and a Rust low-latency retrieval path.
vs hosted memory-API platforms (memory-as-a-service, proprietary engines): Cortex gives the same memory primitives — extraction, supersession, forgetting, memory-injecting router, MCP — but the engine runs inside the customer's own VPC, and connectors aren't paywalled behind an enterprise tier.
vs Microsoft Copilot / Gemini Enterprise (locked to MS/Google ecosystems): model-agnostic, BYO-LLM.
Differentiators: self-hosted + video memory + decisions timeline + permission-parity + open connector SDK.
B4. User Stories (by epic, with acceptance criteria)
Universal Search: search across all sources, ranked/cited, permission-respecting. AC: results never include unauthorized docs (red-team verified); hybrid+rerank; <700 ms p95; source badges + deep links.
Conversational Q&A: AC: streamed answer with progressive citation reveal; abstains when uncertain; every claim cites a deep link.
Ask-in-Slack/Teams: AC: /ask slash command; threaded answer with citations; respects the asker's permissions.
Video Search: AC: transcript snippet + jump-to-timestamp player; speaker attribution.
Expert Finder: AC: "who knows about X" → ranked people with evidence (authored docs/PRs/threads).
Memory/Decisions Timeline: AC: decisions on a topic chronologically; superseded ones flagged.
"What did I miss" digest: AC: personalized daily/weekly summary of relevant activity.
Admin Console: AC: connector config w/ OAuth, sync-health dashboard, permission audit, usage analytics, redaction rules, model config.
API/SDK & MCP: AC: typed SDK; MCP server; browser extension; email-in address.
B5. Core Features

Universal search; conversational Q&A with citations; Slack/Teams bot; browser extension (save + ask on any page); IDE/MCP integration; video search with timestamp jump; "what did I miss" digests; expert finder; memory/decisions timeline; saved collections/spaces; alerts/subscriptions; admin console; API/SDK.

B6. Onboarding / Time-to-Value

Day 0: docker-compose eval or Helm install → connect SSO → connect first 2 sources (Google Drive + Slack) → initial backfill with progress UI → golden-set auto-eval → first cited answer within hours. Targets: first "wow" cited answer < 1 day; full org backfill < 1 week.

B7. Success Metrics
North Star: weekly cited answers accepted per active user.
Activation: ≥1 accepted answer in week 1.
Retention: WAU/MAU > 50%.
Quality: citation accuracy > 90%; thumbs-up rate; abstention correctness.
Coverage: % of org knowledge indexed; sync freshness.
B8. Pricing & Packaging

Self-hosted enterprise: per-seat annual; open-core Community free for small teams; Enterprise tier adds SSO/SCIM, advanced connectors, RBAC, audit, and support. Usage-based add-on for GPU/video-hours. Volume tiers at 1k/10k/50k seats.

B9. UI DESIGN THEME — "Signal"

Point of view: a calm, information-dense situation room for organizational knowledge — editorial clarity over chrome, source provenance always visible, keyboard-first, dark-mode-native. Feels like Linear × a research tool: fast, quiet, precise. Every answer wears its sources on its sleeve.

Typography
UI sans: Inter (or Geist). Scale (size/line-height/weight): display 32/40/600 · h1 24/32/600 · h2 20/28/600 · h3 16/24/600 · body 14/22/400 · body-strong 14/22/500 · small 13/20/400 · caption 12/16/500 · micro 11/14/500.
Mono: JetBrains Mono for code/IDs/error-codes — 13/20.
Spacing / Radii / Elevation / Motion / Icons
8pt system: 2, 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64 (base unit 8).
Radii: sm 6 · md 8 · lg 12 · xl 16 · pill 999 · card 12.
Elevation: e0 none · e1 0 1px 2px rgba(0,0,0,.24) · e2 0 4px 12px rgba(0,0,0,.32) · e3 0 12px 32px rgba(0,0,0,.40).
Motion: fast 120 ms · base 180 ms · slow 240 ms; easing standard cubic-bezier(.2,0,0,1), entrance cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1); honor prefers-reduced-motion.
Icons: Lucide (1.5 px stroke; Phosphor secondary for filled states).
Component Inventory

Search bar (source filter chips + / focus) · result card (title, source badge, highlighted snippet, deep link, timestamp, author avatar) · citation chip (numbered, hover-preview) · source badge · chat thread · streaming answer with progressive citation reveal (superscript citations fade in as tokens arrive, linking to the source panel) · video player with transcript scrubber (click transcript → seek) · connector card (logo, status, last-sync, item count) · sync-health indicator (green/amber/red + sparkline) · empty/loading (skeleton)/error states · command palette (⌘K) · decisions timeline (superseded items struck-through) · expert card.

Layout & Responsive
3-pane desktop: collapsible left nav · center content/chat · right source/citation panel. Breakpoints: sm 640 · md 768 · lg 1024 · xl 1280 · 2xl 1536. Right panel collapses < lg; left nav → drawer < md. Virtualized result/message lists.
Accessibility (WCAG 2.2 AA)

Contrast ≥ 4.5:1 body / 3:1 large (tokens verified); keyboard-first (all actions reachable, ⌘K palette, 2 px accent focus rings); streaming answers use aria-live="polite" with citations announced as "source + link"; reduced motion honored; no motion-only signaling.

Frontend Stack

React 19 + Vite + TypeScript · TanStack Router + TanStack Query · Tailwind v4 with CSS-variable tokens · Radix primitives / Base UI (or shadcn/ui) · Zustand for local UI state · TanStack Virtual for lists · SSE for streaming render · Vitest + Playwright + Storybook.

Key Screens (wireframe descriptions)
Global Search / Home: centered search bar, source filter chips, recent + suggested, ⌘K hint; below, "what's new" digest cards.
Answer / Chat: center streamed answer with inline superscript citations; right panel lists sources with previews; input pinned bottom with source-scope selector.
Result List: virtualized cards; left facet filters (source, time, author, space).
Video Result: player top; synchronized scrolling transcript with speaker labels + highlighted match; "jump to" chips.
Decisions Timeline: vertical timeline by topic; current decision highlighted, superseded struck-through with "superseded by" + provenance links.
Expert Finder: ranked people cards with evidence chips and Slack/contact actions.
Admin — Connectors: grid of connector cards (status/last-sync/items); add-connector OAuth flow.
Admin — Sync Health & Audit: dashboards for freshness, error rates, permission audit log, usage analytics, model config, redaction rules.
B10. Cost Model (rough monthly infra)
1,000 employees: Qdrant with BQ (~10–30 M chunks) on a 16–32 GB RAM node; 1–2×H100 (or BYO-API); modest Postgres/MinIO/NATS → ~$4–8k/mo self-hosted GPU (materially less with BYO-API). Video: $0.50/recording-hr (Recall) + $0.15/hr transcription. WhisperX self-host ≈ $1.28 per 100 audio-hours.
10,000 employees: ~100–300 M chunks (BQ ~20–60 GB RAM); 4–8×H100 fleet + autoscale; larger ClickHouse/Postgres → ~$25–50k/mo. Initial embedding backfill is a one-time spike — smooth over weeks via bounded queues.
B11. Caveats
Slack rate limits materially constrain non-Marketplace ingestion (mitigations in A17).
Self-hosted GPU cost is the dominant TCO driver; BYO-API is the escape hatch.
Knowledge-graph and agentic features add complexity — ship after core retrieval proves value.
Benchmark numbers for LLM serving are third-party and version/hardware-dependent; pin engine versions and re-measure on your own corpus. Contextual retrieval gains vary by domain — validate per corpus before rollout.
Hosted memory platforms publish client SDKs, not engines — their public repos are useful as design references only, so every memory-layer behavior here is specified from first principles rather than inherited.
